description: Ornith-1.5-9B on one rtx-pro-4500-blackwell-32gb with SGLang 0.5.19, reasoning and vision at the model's full 131072-token window. Chat, reasoning, tools and vision accepted. MTP not enabled in this run. Throughput figures are engine-reported and disputed (see metadata.measurements.dispute).

capabilities.chat.reason: omp_accept.py chat probe returned the pinned answer

capabilities.reasoning.reason: omp_accept.py reasoning probe: a separate reasoning_content phase with the answer still in content

capabilities.tools.reason: omp_accept.py tools probe: a forced call with valid arguments and a round-tripped tool result

capabilities.vision.reason: omp_accept.py vision probe: solid red and blue PNGs named correctly

engine.version.reason: sglang.launch_server served from the pinned ghcr.io/0xsero/sglang image; the in-container version probe could not resolve a Python path, so the 0.5.19 tag carried from the plan is unconfirmed

launch.image.reason: upstream release image pulled by digest on the rented card

serving.max_context_tokens.reason: the window the loaded server was configured with and served on; the sweep covers shorter prompts and records every attempted row

acceptance.harness: omp_accept.py (identity, chat, reasoning, tools, vision) + tabby_sweep.py

findings: Throughput: decode_tok_s_per_stream and the derived metrics.peak_generation_tps are TabbyAPI server-reported per-request decode rates, not client-timed aggregate throughput (raw sweep rows carry decode_tok_s_aggregate=null). peak_generation_tps has been nulled in the speed-sweep; per-row values are retained verbatim as raw evidence.

Decode-only vs end-to-end: the reported per-stream decode rate excludes prefill/queue time. Client end-to-end throughput is far lower (Flash-Next 262144/C4: 512 tokens in 452.8 s = 1.13 tok/s versus the 22.95 tok/s per-stream headline).

Concurrency: the previous serving.max_concurrency was a queued request count, not a certified capability, so the claim is dropped (serving.max_concurrency=null). Only client-side timestamps are available: at the advertised long window the admitted request streams did not overlap in wall-clock (observed_client_stream_overlap=1) - identical prompt_time and completion_time across C1/C2/C4, TTFT and elapsed scaling linearly, aggregate tok/s flat (e.g. Flash-Next 262144 ~3.37 at C1 vs ~3.38 at C4) - while at 32768 up to 2 client streams overlapped. Client intervals can show queue/overlap behaviour but CANNOT certify the engine's internal GPU batch, which is unknown without engine-side instrumentation.
sweep_rows.accepted counts completed benchmark rows, not acceptance probes; it is not an acceptance verdict and must not be read next to metadata.acceptance.

MTP acceptance: acceptance_rate was engine-log-derived (drafted-vs-accepted speculative token counts parsed from server logs), not independently client-verified. Raw counts preserved under metadata.measurements.mtp.engine_reported; the derived rate is nulled.

Cache state: TabbyAPI sweep requests were cold - prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens=0 in every raw record - so the raw 'cache_state: unverified' label understates what the data shows; no warm-cache measurement exists. This is a derived observation only: the immutable raw records are not edited, and any enrichment must come from an auditable separate transform, never a hand edit.

Latency: the SGLang sweep carries no latency data - all 21 rows have decode_tok_s_per_stream=null and ttft=null, only elapsed. Its cold/warm pairs differ 2-5x, so no Ornith row is comparable to a TabbyAPI cold-only row.

mtp.reason: MTP not enabled in this run: the SGLang serve_argv carried no speculative/draft/eagle flags and the sweep rows.jsonl/manifest.json recorded no mtp/draft/spec field. Whether Ornith-1.5-9B ships an MTP/draft head for SGLang was not tested; the earlier claim that it 'ships no MTP head' is not evidenced and is marked unverified.

concurrency_observed.admission_behaviour: not measurable - the SGLang sweep recorded no per-row latency (decode/ttft null), only elapsed
concurrency_observed.basis: client-side per-stream first/last-token timestamps only, not engine instrumentation; DELIVERY-24.md protocol section 3.4 defines the engine-instrumented overlap measurement for re-measurement
concurrency_observed.engine_batch: unknown - not certifiable without engine-side instrumentation
